message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty noir to high‑stakes heists—and have been praised by critics and audiences alike.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | A courtroom drama that blends historical fact with sharp dialogue, capturing the tension of the 1969 trial. |
| 2 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | A sprawling saga of organized crime, featuring De Niro’s groundbreaking de-aging tech and a stellar ensemble. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced humor meets a complex plot about drug empire ownership. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A psychological thriller that examines how a false accusation can destroy lives. |
| 5 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror story, blending suspense with social commentary. |
| 6 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A brutal, atmospheric revenge story set in 19th‑century Australia. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned crime‑thriller, with a strong focus on gender dynamics. |
| 8 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A tense cat‑and‑mouse chase between two detectives investigating a serial killer. |
| 9 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Ethan Hawke | A bleak, atmospheric crime drama that explores the roots of violence in rural America. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror story, blending suspense with social commentary. |

> **Note:** Some of these films were released on streaming platforms (e.g., *The Irishman* on Netflix) rather than in theaters due to the pandemic. If you’re looking for a specific sub‑genre or a particular style within crime‑thrillers, let me know and I can refine the list further!
